topic_title: Phishing Indicators a SOC L1 Must Recognize
topic_summary: Quick-pivot indicators that turn 'just another email' into an actionable incident.

flashcards.front: Name three high-signal envelope indicators in a phishing email.
flashcards.back: 1) Sender domain ≠ reply-to / mailfrom, 2) SPF/DKIM/DMARC failure, 3) Recently registered or look-alike sender domain.
Tricking a user into granting an OAuth app excessive scopes (e.g., Mail.Read on Microsoft 365); no password is stolen but the attacker keeps access until the consent is revoked.

flashcards.front: Why does opening a phishing URL in an isolated browser help triage?
flashcards.back: It detonates payloads, captures redirects, and shows the final landing page without exposing the analyst's identity or the corporate browser session.

questions.stem: Which SPF/DKIM/DMARC outcome is most suspicious on a high-priority email?

options.label: B
options.content: DKIM passes, SPF passes, DMARC fails (alignment mismatch)

options.label: C
options.content: DMARC is not configured by sender

options.label: D
options.content: DKIM signature missing because of mailing-list rewrite

questions.explanation: Alignment failure (passing protocols but failing DMARC alignment) is a strong spoofing indicator. Missing DMARC config and list-rewrite cases happen on legitimate mail too.

questions.stem: A user reports they 'accepted some permission popup' from a Microsoft login screen and now spam is being sent from their account. The most likely root cause is…

options.label: B
options.content: Consent phishing — revoke the malicious OAuth app

questions.explanation: Consent phishing leaves credentials untouched but grants the attacker token-level access until the application consent is revoked in the tenant.

questions.stem: Select two safer ways for an L1 analyst to inspect a suspicious phishing URL.

options.label: A
options.content: Open it in an isolated browser / browser-in-a-box service

options.label: B
options.content: Submit it to a URL sandbox (e.g., urlscan.io)

options.label: C
options.content: Click it from the corporate workstation

options.label: D
options.content: Forward it to the executive team for review

questions.explanation: Isolated browsers and URL sandboxes let you detonate safely. Clicking from corp or fanning out to execs both increase blast radius.
